A widespread outage hit Microsoft platforms including Outlook on Thursday, with many users encountering trouble using their email accounts and other errors across the tech giant's suite of apps.
Nearly 130,000 users on outage tracker Downdetector reported problems accessing Outlook just after 1 p.m. ET. New reports have since fallen from that peak, but many said they couldn't send and receive emails or had trouble loading their inboxes altogether.

item.title: What's a Honey Trap? The spy tactic that helped topple Jensen Huang
item.description:
National
What's a Honey Trap? The spy tactic that helped topple Jensen Huang
November 12, 20265:45 PM ET
Frank Langfitt
A screengrab from CTI video footage obtained November 9, 2026 shows a woman identified by Reuters as Alice Huang after comparison with a photograph obtained separately, attending a dinner with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (in black) at a restaurant in Taipei, Taiwan on May 22, 2025.
CTI via Reuters
hide caption
toggle caption i
CTI via Reuters
One of the world's oldest spy tactics appears to have helped topple one of the world's richest men. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday amid revelations that he had an affair with a female client that U.S. intelligence identified as a Chinese spy, according to the New York Times.
NPR has not independently confirmed the reporting by the Times, which said Huang also had an unrelated affair with a company executive who reported to him. The Chinese government has called the accusation of spying, "nothing but smears against China."
Using a romantic relationship to gather intelligence from foreigners – known as a honey trap – has a long history in China and beyond. The Chinese Ministry of State Security, the country's main civilian intelligence agency, routinely tries to recruit women and occasionally men for honey traps,...

item.title: 'Punch in the gut': Homes sales fall to their lowest in 16 years
item.description:
Business
'Punch in the gut': Homes sales fall to their lowest in 16 years
November 12, 20261:44 PM ET
By
Stephan Bisaha
Home sales fell to their lowest since 2010, a new report shows, in large part due to high mortgage rates.
Mario Tama/Getty Images
hide caption
toggle caption i
Mario Tama/Getty Images
The housing market has finally broken out of the stagnant holding pattern it's been stuck in for more than four years – just not in the right direction.
News
Homelessness in the U.S. saw its largest drop in more than a decade last year
Existing home sales in October fell to 3.75 million, making an 8.8% decline in sales from a year earlier, according to the National Association of Realtors. The last time sales were this low was 16 years ago.
"It was a punch in the gut," said Joel Berner, senior economist at Realtor.com. "We expected to see a soft month but not the softest month since 2010."
Expensive mortgages are a big factor
The drop is mainly due to high mortgage rates.

item.description:

Casualties continue to rise after Brooklyn building collapses
November 12, 20261:15 PM ET
By
NPR Staff
A view of the site where a building collapsed in Brooklyn, New York on Wednesday.
Yuki Iwamura/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Yuki Iwamura/AP
The New York City Fire Department reported Thursday that more victims had been found after a three-story residential building in the Flatbush neighborhood of Brooklyn collapsed a day earlier.
Mayor Zohran Mamdani said six people had been declared dead at the scene. Two others died in a hospital. 18 other people were injured in the building collapse.
Search efforts are continuing with more than 250 firefighters and emergency workers deployed to the site, according to city officials.

item.description:

The SS United States takes its final voyage to the bottom of the Gulf of Mexico
November 12, 202611:20 AM ET
By
Ruby Siefken
Retired passenger liner SS United States is pictured at a dock in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The SS United States still holds the east- and west-bound transatlantic crossing records. AFP PHOTO/JEWEL SAMAD (Photo credit should read JEWEL SAMAD/AFP via Getty Images)
JEWEL SAMAD/AFP via Getty Images/AFP
hide caption
toggle caption i
JEWEL SAMAD/AFP via Getty Images/AFP
A giant ship sunk off the coast of Florida yesterday—and the coast guard didn't do a thing to stop it.
The SS United States is a retired ocean liner that was deliberately sunk on Wednesday to create the world's largest artificial reef. After hours of slow descent, it finally disappeared beneath the waves at 10 p.m. ET last night. It now rests 180 feet beneath the surface at the bottom of the Gulf of Mexico in an upright position.
Measuring almost 1,000 feet from bow to stern, the giant ship is longer than the Titanic. After it's settled on the ocean floor, the ship's hundreds of rooms, corridors and elevator shafts will become a deep-sea playground for divers, fish and other aquatic life.

item.description:

By
Jaclyn Diaz
,

Local and federal law enforcement respond to reports of an active shooting on Thursday in Washington.
Tom Brenner/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Tom Brenner/AP
Busy morning crowds in Washington, D.C.'s Logan Circle ran for cover Thursday after a gunman opened fire at a local gym, VIDA Fitness, killing at least one person and injuring at least four others.
The gunman left the gym area, entered a nearby apartment building where he barricaded himself. Jeffery W. Carroll, the interim Police Chief of the Metropolitan Police Department, who briefed the public this morning, said at the time of the briefing that the shooter had shot himself.
A police spokeswoman later confirmed to NPR that the gunman died.
The gunman shot and killed one person inside the gym and injured another in the lobby or alley area of the building, Carroll said. The other three victims were shot across the street at a construction site, he said. One person remains in critical condition.
